title: Normalized finite scalar reduction map
statement: Let l be prime, let E and L be finite extensions of Q_l, and let iota:E -> L be a Q_l-algebra embedding. For F=E,L fix its valuation ring and uniformizer. On the small pro-etale site of a scheme W, put R_F,W=lim_m (O_F/pi_F^(m+1))_W, A_F,W=(O_F/pi_F^(n+1))_W, p_F:R_F,W -> A_F,W the quotient projection, j_W:R_E,W -> R_L,W the completed scalar map, and k_W:A_E,W -> A_L,W the quotient scalar map. Thus p_E;k_W=j_W;p_L. Write S_W(M)=R_L,W tensor_(R_E,W) M and T_F,W(M)=A_F,W tensor_(R_F,W) M, with sheafified ordinary tensor, their canonical unit sections denoted 1 tensor x. Restriction of scalars is understood along the displayed ring maps. All complexes below are arbitrary unbounded cochain complexes with termwise ordinary scalar extension and reduction. For every n and every R_E,W-module sheaf M there is exactly one A_E,W-linear map b_M:T_E,W(M) -> Res_kW T_L,W(S_W(M)) satisfying b_M(1 tensor x)=1 tensor (1 tensor x) for every object U and section x of M over U. No local freeness, flatness or boundedness assumption is imposed. These coefficient, module and tensor constructions use [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], [def-sfb-scalar-extension-pure-tensor-section], [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

proof.text: Use compatibility of the completed scalar map with its quotient projections to identify p_E;k with j;p_L. Transfer the ordinary extension/restriction adjunction for p_E to the chosen unrestricted finite reduction functor using its tensor presentation.

For M compose the scalar unit M -> Res_j S(M) with the restricted target-reduction unit S(M) -> Res_pL T_L S(M). Identify both restriction actions along the coefficient square and transpose through T_E dashv Res_pE. Its unit equation gives the desired formula on 1 tensor x. A morphism out of T_E is determined by these sections by the same adjunction, proving uniqueness. Applying that test to a module morphism gives naturality; applying it to differentials constructs the termwise chain map and natural transformation used by both consumers.
